item.title: Netherlands player ratings vs Germany: Denzel Dumfries endures a nightmare as Xavi's Oranje lose top spot in Nations League thrashing
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-GER-NED - AFP The Netherlands only needed to avoid defeat in Berlin to finish top of Nations League Group A2, but Germany tore them apart in a 5-0 win that handed Xavi Hernandez his first defeat as head coach. The visitors had the better of the early chances, with Crysencio Summerville slipping as he prepared to shoot and Donyell Malen heading a glorious opportunity over the bar. Derry Scherhant punished them in the 41st minute, cutting inside from the left and firing into the top corner. Germany struck four times in 17 minutes after the break. Florian Wirtz curled in from 25 yards on the hour, Nico Schlotterbeck headed in Brajan Gruda's free-kick five minutes later, Wirtz added his second in the 71st minute and Gruda completed the scoring in the 77th. Germany finished with 10 shots on target to the Netherlands' one, and their first win at the Olympiastadion since 2010 lifted them above the Dutch into first place, although both sides still go through to the quarter-finals. Goalkeeper & Defence Bart Verbruggen (5/10): Got his fingertips to Scherhant's opener but could not keep it out, and was left badly exposed once Germany cut loose in the second half. Made five saves, including stops from Kai Havertz, Gruda and Aleksandar Pavlovic, but his push onto the post from Scherhant's shot fell kindly for Gruda to score the fifth. Called his team-mates into an angry huddle straight after. Denzel Dumfries (3/10): The captain was at the centre of Germany's first three goals. He failed to get tight to Scherhant for the opener, the ball came back to Wirtz off him before the second, and his foul on Scherhant gave away the free-kick from which Schlotterbeck headed in the third. Did get forward to head over at the back post early in the second half. Micky van de Ven (5/10): Timed a challenge on Wirtz in the box perfectly midway through the first half, having already been penalised for bundling over Havertz. Like the rest of the defence, though, he could not cope with Germany's movement after the break. Worked hard as Germany took over the midfield and made a fine sliding tackle to stop Younes Ebnoutalib from shooting in the 82nd minute. Ruben van Bommel (6/10): Livelier than most after replacing Gakpo in the 79th minute, having two shots blocked and racing down the left to try a cross that Jonathan Tah cut out. Xavi Hernandez (3/10): Suffered his first defeat as Netherlands head coach on the night his side only needed a draw to top the group. His team made a bright start but fell apart after the break, conceding four times in 17 minutes.

item.title: Scherhant elated after rout of the Netherlands: "It was so much fun"
item.description: Scherhant elated after rout of the Netherlands: "It was so much fun" Netting a goal in his home city of Berlin, Derry Scherhant could hardly put Germany's 5-0 win over the Netherlands into words. “What can I say? I don't think it could have gone any better,” the SC Freiburg winger said in his post-match interview with ARD. "You couldn't have dreamed of anything better, really. It's just unbelievable. It was so much fun and I'm just absolutely delighted.” Having turned 24 last Tuesday but busy with the DFB squad, Scherhant revealed he felt this game would be the perfect birthday present. "Absolutely, yeah, there are plans. I'd already manifested beforehand that things would go well, and I've organised something. A nice meal with all my friends and family, and I'm looking forward to it. I mean, it couldn't have gone any better here in my city. “To score the opening goal as well, I'm very happy, very proud. And it's just so enjoyable playing football with the lads,” he added.

item.title: Lindsey Vonn Shares Gruesome Video of Doctors Using Power Tools on Her Leg During 5-Hour Surgery
item.description: Lindsey Vonn shares updates after her ninth surgery to repair damage from her Winter Olympics crash Credit: Lindsey Vonn/Instagram NEED TO KNOW Lindsey Vonn shared a grisly look into her surgery The Olympic skier’s ninth surgery removed hardware from her left leg and replaced her torn ACL Vonn waited nine months for her bone to heal after crashes at a World Cup race and the Milan Games Lindsey Vonn ’s surgeons had to upgrade their equipment to get her leg back in working order. As Vonn, 42, recovers from her ninth surgery to repair the damage she sustained in her two crashes during the 2026 Winter Olympics and a World Cup race a week earlier, she’s sharing a behind-the-scenes — and often gruesome — look at her time on the surgeon’s table. On Sunday, Nov. 15, four days after her five-hour-long surgery, the five-time Olympian shared a video of doctors using a power drill to remove the plates and screws that have kept her left leg in place since her February crashes. “What power tools are made for 💪🏻,” Vonn captioned the video on her Instagram Stories. The post had multiple warnings about the sensitive content, as it showed her leg cut open and pulled apart with forceps so a doctor could unscrew the plates with the drill. Lindsey Vonn shows the screws that were removed from her leg Credit: Lindsey Vonn/Instagram The 84-time World Cup winner had been training and preparing for this surgery, an ACL replacement, for the last few months. Vonn had “completely” torn her ACL during a World Cup event on Jan. 30, a week before she was set to compete at the Milan Games. She decided to race anyway , but just a few seconds into her run in the women’s downhill final, she clipped a gate and crashed, leading to a complex tibia fracture in the same leg. Vonn was airlifted to a nearby hospital and underwent her first four surgeries to stabilize her leg, before being transported back to the U.S. for additional treatment. This ninth surgery, which Vonn was “praying” would be her last, involved “basically removing all the hardware so we can put in a new ACL, because I don’t have an ACL still. Cause of all the plates, we just couldn’t put it in,” she explained in a video she scheduled to go live during the procedure. “So I’ve been waiting all of these nine months so my bone could heal and we could fix the ACL, and my bones healed, which is great news. But obviously now that means another six to nine months [of recovery] like a normal ACL [surgery]. item.title: Colts’ Shane Steichen insists $88 million whiff isn’t why Daniel Jones hasn’t been benched
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Colts’ Shane Steichen insists $88 million whiff isn’t why Daniel Jones hasn’t been benched appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts snapped a five-game losing streak on Sunday after defeating the Miami Dolphins 24-22 in Week 10. Despite the victory, many are still wondering why Daniel Jones has yet to be benched after he had another lackluster performance. On Monday, head coach Shane Steichen opened up about continuing to play Jones instead of giving someone else on the roster a chance. At one point, Steichen was asked if Jones’ $88 million contract has played a part in the 29-year-old’s playing time, according to James Boyd of The Athletic. Steichen shut down the question entirely , claiming he isn’t “going to get into contract stuff” with media members. Instead, the fourth-year coach claimed that, although the Colts want Jones to improve in taking care of the ball, one of the key reasons why he hasn’t been benched is because the eight-year veteran does a good job of preparing the team for each game every week, per Boyd. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “There’s a lot of things that play into it,” Steichen said. ‘Obviously, we know, he knows he’s gotta take care of the ball better… But he does lead our team each and every week to get ready… I think it’s not all about one guy. I think it takes all 11 to do their job at a high level. It starts with me as a play-caller, calling better plays to make sure guys are getting open and separating.” #Colts HC Shane Steichen , asked what Daniel Jones is doing on *game days* to remain the starter: “There’s a lot of things that play into it. Obviously, we know, he knows he’s gotta take care of the ball better. … But he does lead our team each and every week to get ready …” pic.twitter.com/8zn47ih3eF — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) November 16, 2026 Daniel Jones had yet another stinker of a performance on Sunday, despite the Colts earning the win over the Dolphins. The former first-round pick ended the day with just 108 passing yards, a touchdown, and two interceptions while completing 50.0% of his pass attempts. Through 10 games played this year, that brings Jones’ season totals to 1,830 yards, seven touchdowns, and a league-high 12 interceptions. He also owns a career-worst 59.6% completion percentage. item.title: Barcelona set maximum Pedro Porro offer
item.description: Barcelona set maximum Pedro Porro offer The board at La Liga giants Barcelona have put a maximum financial outlay in place, amid hopes of bringing in Pedro Porro from Tottenham Hotspur. This comes amid an ongoing search on the part of the Blaugrana for reinforcements at right-back. With Jules Koundé having seemingly lost the trust of manager Hansi Flick, Barca are currently on the lookout for a potential replacement for the French international. A player with a particular set of characteristics is being sought, one boasting experience, without being too close to the twilight years of his career. The aforementioned Pedro Porro appears to fit this bill, 27 years of age, a full Spanish international, and with experience of joining forces with Lamine Yamal down the right wing. Barcelona, however, will not pay over the odds for the Spurs man… As per a report from Fichajes , citing Diario Sport, owing to financial constraints heading into the January transfer window: ‘Barcelona could spend a maximum of €50 million.’ It is also noted, though, significantly, that ‘the player’s only desire is to join Barcelona’. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Club president meets Arsenal star’s entourage to propose move
item.description: Club president meets Arsenal star’s entourage to propose move Mikel Merino has emerged as a serious transfer target for Atletico Madrid , with the Spanish club already holding discussions with his representatives over a potential return to Spain. The midfielder is currently happy at Arsenal, where he is regarded as an important member of the squad, and the Gunners would prefer to keep him. However, Arsenal could consider selling Merino if the right offer arrives. Although he remains a valuable player, the club may not view him as irreplaceable, meaning a suitable proposal could persuade them to sanction his departure during one of the upcoming transfer windows. Atletico Madrid appear keen to take advantage of the situation and bring the Spanish midfielder back to his homeland. His experience and quality could make him an attractive addition to their squad as they look to strengthen their options. Atletico Madrid step up their interest According to Fichajes , Atletico president Enrique Cerezo has already made contact with Merino’s representatives as he explores the possibility of securing a transfer. The report claims that Cerezo has held two separate discussions with the midfielder’s entourage, demonstrating the Spanish club’s determination to pursue an agreement. Their interest suggests that they are serious about bringing the Arsenal player back to Spain. Atletico believe the World Cup winner has the quality and experience to add value to their current squad. They are therefore keen to complete a deal as soon as possible, although negotiations with Arsenal could prove challenging if the Gunners demand a significant transfer fee. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) Arsenal could consider a suitable offer Merino is not expected to push for an exit, particularly given his current happiness at the Emirates. Arsenal also have reasons to retain him, considering his importance to the squad and the contribution he makes to the team. Nevertheless, the situation could change if Atletico Madrid submits an attractive proposal. Arsenal may be willing to consider the offer rather than automatically reject the possibility of selling him. Should the Gunners decide to sanction his departure, they would also need to identify a suitable replacement. item.title: Florian Wirtz reveals Germany's relentless attacking mentality after Netherlands thrashing
item.description: Florian Wirtz reveals Germany's relentless attacking mentality after Netherlands thrashing Germany rounded off their 2026 international calendar in emphatic fashion on Monday evening, dismantling the Netherlands at Olympiastadion to secure the top spot in their Nations League group. Derry Scherhant's superb first-half opener set the hosts on their way before a devastating second-half display saw Florian Wirtz score twice, with Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda also getting on the scoresheet. Speaking to ARD after his 50th international appearance, Wirtz touched on the attacking mentality in the second half, revealing that Germany had no intention of sitting back and protecting their advantage. “I think we want to stand four playing attacking football,” said the Liverpool midfielder. "We always want to score goals and dominate our opponents. “We wanted to keep pressing forward and score more goals. And I think we did that perfectly.” The 23-year-old also admitted that Germany had enjoyed themselves considerably more after the break, having initially struggled to find space against their Dutch opponents. "Of course, we hope that we can bring the fans a lot of enjoyment. And for us, it was also a lot of fun," Wirtz explained. "Especially in the second half. The first half still involved quite a lot of hard work and a lot of running. "In the second half, everything was a little bit easier because we had more space. And that's when it became really enjoyable." Reflecting on their progress after sealing their third win under Klopp, Wirtz was equally optimistic about what lies ahead. "It's definitely a fitting way to finish, I'd say, and one that we're very happy with. "We want to carry on like this next year. That's clear. We want to improve. "I think we've definitely already taken some good steps forward in our development as a team. “I'm very proud and happy to be part of this team, and it's really enjoyable.”

item.title: Nwaneri and Moore guide England U21 to friendly win over France U21
item.description: Nwaneri and Moore guide England U21 to friendly win over France U21 Two-time European championship holders England U21 end 2026 with a 3-2 win over France in Bristol. Bundesliga youngsters Mikey Moore and Ethan Nwaneri shone as Lee Carsley's side recovered from their defeat to Afonso Moreira's Portugal at the same venue. Köln's attacker opened the scoring for the hosts from Nwaneri's assist in the sixth minute. Borussia Dortmund’s attacker added another direct goal contribution when Divin Mubama doubled 4England's advantage at the half-hour mark. Both Moore and Nwaneri could return to their parent clubs Tottenham Hotspur and Arsenal, respectively, in January as the North London clubs aren't satisfied with their spells so far in the Bundesliga. France leveled the score with two late goals before Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation Max Dowman won it for England with his first goal at this level in the 89th-minute. Moore's Köln teammate Jahmai Simpson-Pusey played the second-half for England U21. France, who have RB Leipzig's duo Abdoul Kone and Tidiam Gomis on their ranks, narrowly lost both of their friendly games after securing their place in the next summer's Euros.

item.title: Wirtz has fun as Germany run riot over Netherlands
item.description: Germany's Florian Wirtz celebrates his side's big win over the Netherlands in Berlin. (Odd ANDERSEN) Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday. Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to shreds in the most impressive match of Jurgen Klopp's six-game stint as coach. It was Germany's biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959. "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second-half," Wirtz told German broadcaster ARD. The Dutch defeat was the first since their coach Xavi Hernandez took charge but, despite Greece's 1-0 win over Serbia on Monday, they also qualified for the final eight, although the last German goal dropped them to second in the group. The Netherlands offered little in attack after Germany's second and missed injured captain Virgil van Dijk at the back, with the hosts cutting through a flimsy defence at will. So often criticised for a lack of end product since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, Wirtz has scored in four in his past four games for Germany. Germany knew only a victory would give them a realistic chance of reaching the quarters, with coach Klopp describing the match as a "final." The game, a rematch of the 1974 World Cup final won by Germany in Munich, began with both sides risk averse and reluctant to move forward. The Dutch had the first good chance when Jurrien Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away. Just after the half hour, the Berlin-born-and-raised Scherhant latched onto a cross from Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu but hit the far post. Nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same blade of grass and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the post. The Germans continued their assault on the Dutch penalty area after the break, Wirtz adding another with a solo effort on the hour. The Liverpool winger dribbled from left to right and back centrally before lifting a shot in off the left post from the penalty arc. Schlotterbeck headed in from a Gruda free-kick with 65 minutes gone. The RB Leipzig winger laid on another goal six minutes later when he tore down the right and found Wirtz, who hammered in off the bottom of the crossbar. In his first Germany match on home soil, Gruda then added one of his own, tapping in a Scherhant shot which rebounded off the post. "We don't mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz. "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team." dwi/pb

item.title: Commanders’ Dan Quinn gives Laremy Tunsil injury update, but return isn’t near
item.description: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Commanders’ Dan Quinn gives Laremy Tunsil injury update, but return isn’t near appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders have had some time to enjoy their win over the Giants. And Jayden Daniels saved his unbeaten record against the Giants with a late TD. However, Daniels won’t get his protector back soon , according to Dan Quinn ’s injury update on Laremy Tunsil via a post on X by Zach Selby. “Quinn said Laremy Tunsil had a good visit with the doctor in his last visit and is about to transition into the strength phase of his rehab. No updates on whether he will play this year, though.” Tunsil got hurt before the season began. His triceps injury was expected to keep him out for the entire season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Commanders still trying to get help from LT Laremy Tunsil The Commanders didn’t get one snap from Tunsil this season. But he has been active, trying to help the team’s young linemen, according to Commanders.com. “I think it’s been a blessing,” tackle Josh Conerly said. “And it means a lot to us, as a group and for me personally. You can talk to him about anything. It’s unreal. I’m very thankful…really just to have a brother, a real brother, that I can lean on no matter what.” Quinn said Tunsil has especially taken Conerly under his wing. “Laremy…has such a good connection with Josh, and checking in, seeing where it’s at, that’s a big deal,” Quinn said in September. But it’s not just Conerly. Guard Chris Paul has received the benefits of Tunsil’s help. “He just has a wonderful spirit, and you can tell the way he just sort of quietly spreads his cheer around the building,” Paul said. “I think he’s just a great example. “He was (on the sideline for the season opener), just active,” Paul said. “Just asking me, ‘What are you seeing? Here’s the type of look this guy’s giving you.’ He’s obviously doing that for both our tackles as well. It’s just been a great source of mentorship for everybody. “He is the top and the pinnacle of the game. Playing next to him has been one of the greatest honors of my life.”

item.title: Deshawndre Washington waives extradition to face charges
item.description: Former New Mexico State University men's basketball player Deshawndre Washington waived extradition and will remain jailed at a Virginia county detention center until he returns to Las Cruces for trial. Washington was taken into custody for an out-of-state warrant by U.S. Marshals in Lebanon on Nov. 15 and placed into custody in Loudoun County Adult Detention Center in Virginia at 11:09 a.m. on Nov. 15. He waived extradition during a Nov. 16 arraignment hearing, according to the Loudoun County Sheriff's Office. His next hearing is scheduled for Nov. 30 unless New Mexico authorities take him into custody and return him to Doña Ana County to face criminal charges before that time, according to the Loudoun County Sheriff's Department. Washington faces multiple felony sexual assault charges for allegedly assaulting former teammates and student managers during the 2022-2023 basketball season. Washington is charged with six counts of criminal sexual contact (aided by another), five counts of conspiracy to commit criminal sexual contact in the fourth degree, one count of conspiracy to commit criminal sexual contact (aided by another) and seven counts of conspiracy to commit false imprisonment and false imprisonment. Third Judicial District Court Judge Conrad Perea issued a bench warrant on Aug. 3 when Washington didn't appear for a scheduled jury trial. During a Nov. 9 motion hearing , Washington, who was playing professional basketball in Lebanon, testified virtually to the court that his passport was removed by authorities in August, preventing him from international travel. Dulles International Airport is in Loudon County but the Sun-News could not confirm that the U.S. Marshal's returned Washington to the U.S. via that airport. The New Mexico Department of Justice is currently working through the logistics of getting Washington back to New Mexico. There was not a hearing scheduled in 3rd Judicial District Court as of late afternoon on Nov. 16. Jason Groves covers local government and politics for the Sun-News. Reach him by email at jgroves@lcsun-news.com . This article originally appeared on Las Cruces Sun-News: Deshawndre Washington waives extradition to face charges

item.title: Strasbourg enquire over Swansea head coach Vitor Matos
item.description: Strasbourg enquire over Swansea head coach Vitor Matos RC Strasbourg have approached EFL Championship side Swansea City for their manager, Vitor Matos, should Hugo Oliveira were to depart the Alsatians, according to a report from The Athletic . The Portuguese manager’s record in Ligue 1 is quite underwhelming since his appointment to replace Ipswich Town-bound Gary O’Neill last summer. Strasbourg won three, drew one and lost six Ligue 1 games with Oliveira at the helm. L’Equipe previously reported that Strasbourg sounded out replacements for Oliveira. After a chastening three-game losing streak, RC Strasbourg regained a bit of confidence in early November with a a 5-1 win over Will Still’s Auxerre, but the Alsatians then suffered a 3-1 away loss to Toulouse, leaving them only two points clear of the relegation zone. The Athletic understands that Matos is keen to take over at the BlueCo-owned Ligue 1 side. Should Hugo Oliveira were to be sacked, he’d be the the fourth manager to be dismissed this Ligue 1 season, after Lens’ Dino Toppmöller, Le Havre’s Didier Digard and Lens’ Yannick Cahuzac, who happens to have been replaced by Digard. Strasbourg host Brest on Saturday. GFFN | Bastien Cheval

item.title: Dan Campbell Set to Address Media, Give Update on Aidan Hutchinson
item.description: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell is expected to provide an important update on Aidan Hutchinson when he meets with reporters on Tuesday, November 17. With the Lions returning from Germany following Sunday’s 35-10 victory over the New England Patriots, Campbell’s first media availability of the week will come one day later than usual. The Lions were given Monday off following their international trip, meaning Campbell did not hold his customary day-after-game press conference. Instead, he is scheduled to address the media Tuesday, when he is reportedly expected to discuss Hutchinson’s knee injury and potentially provide more information about the star defensive end’s status. And considering what has been reported over the past 24 hours, Lions fans will certainly be paying close attention. Nov 13, 2026; Munich, Germany; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell at press conference at FC Bayern Campus. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dan Campbell Expected to Address Aidan Hutchinson Injury Hutchinson suffered a serious right knee injury during the first quarter of Sunday’s victory in Munich after celebrating a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. The 26-year-old jumped into the air following the play, landed awkwardly, and immediately grabbed his knee before receiving medical attention. He was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the game and was later spotted using crutches while leaving the stadium. Following the game, Campbell acknowledged that the Lions did not yet have a definitive update on Hutchinson’s condition. “Nothing new. We’ll know more when we get back in the States,” Campbell told reporters Sunday. “But anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate that he is, he’s a captain of ours, that doesn’t make things easy.” Since those comments, the situation has become increasingly concerning. According to Ian Rapoport’s Monday injury report , initial testing indicated Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his right knee, an injury expected to end his 2026 season. There is also concern about possible meniscus damage, with additional testing planned following the team’s return to the United States. item.title: Jmariyae Robinson breaking records, making memories for Missouri State
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — In the ever-changing college sports landscape, one-program players have been few and far between. For Missouri State, one sticks out more than most. Wide receiver Jmariyae Robinson is smashing Missouri State records and creating memories for fans inside Plaster Stadium. Against New Mexico State, Robinson caught a crucial touchdown before halftime. He celebrates with a few young Missouri State fans in the end zone. Robinson has continually made plays throughout his five year career with the Bears and has solidified himself as the best. Missouri State soccer: Bears make NCAA Tournament as at-large bid Robinson’s big touchdown catch gave him the most receiving yards in Missouri State history. It also helped him tie for the most receiving touchdowns, too. Robinson has 2,227 yards to his name, while he’s snagged 17 touchdowns in a Bears uniform. Robinson already earned the title for most receptions in a career earlier in the season. He is now the owner of the triple crown, but one more touchdown will put him alone at the top of the record list. “Less than half of the guys that transfer more than once are graduating college, which is insane. J-Rob is fixing to graduate,” Missouri State coach Casey Woods said. “He’s going to hold these records. He’s a selfless player.” Every season has been better than his last. Robinson has a career-high 54 receptions this season. He has 508 receiving yards, 124 yards shy of his best mark set last season. Robinson will look to increase his touchdown total with two more games left in the season. Longtime teammate Connor Lair has seen Robinson’s work up close and has been impressed each and every day. “Coming in at the same time and knowing each other each year, he’s a great guy,” Lair said. “He deserves all of the recognition that he gets.” Missouri State football: How the Bears won its first home OT game in history Becoming the triple crown owner has always been Robinson’s goal. Before the season, he talked about wanting the title of being the best wide receiver in school history. “I want to finish what I started,” Robinson said earlier in the year. “I could be number one in touchdowns, receptions and yards. I would like to accomplish that, as well as having a winning season with the same people I started with.” Robinson and the Bears (4-6, 3-3 in CUSA) have a stern test against Jacksonville State (7-3, 5-1) away from home at 1 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 21. item.title: San Francisco 49ers TE George Kittle Publicly Trolls Cowboys After Week 10 Win
item.description: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 15: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers looks on prior to a game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers found themselves in a shootout with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday but still emerged victorious. San Francisco held a three-score lead at one point but allowed Dallas to climb back into the game. Despite the late comeback, the 49ers escaped AT&T Stadium with a 46-40 win behind star quarterback Brock Purdy and running back Christian McCaffrey, who both went ballistic. Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns. Two of those scores went to McCaffrey, who recorded three touchdowns himself while hauling in four receptions for 161 yards. George Kittle Publicly Trolls Cowboys Another 49er who made a major impact was tight end George Kittle, who caught six passes for 74 yards. Kittle continues to find success against the Cowboys, and after going viral last year for wearing the “[explicit] Dallas” shirt under his pads, he decided not to flaunt it too much this time. However, he wore it once again. He posted several photos of him and his teammates from the game with a caption that read, “… Dallas,” while labeling the location as “Jerry’s World.” And if you look closely at the collage of photos Kittle shared, you’ll see him pull down the “[explicit] Dallas” shirt to show everybody he had it on. Check it out: View this post on Instagram 49ers Fans React on Social Media “Hell yea Georgie!! I knew you’d have that shirt on,” a fan said. Someone else added, “I knew that shirt was on lmao.” Another person wrote, “I KNEW YOU HAD THE SHIRT ON!!!” “So, the gray shirt is 4-0 now?!” one more fan commented. Looking at the 49ers Right Now San Francisco is firing on all cylinders, and while its defense looked a bit suspect, the Cowboys offense has the capabilities to be one of the best in the NFL when it gets into a rhythm. Dallas certainly played well down the stretch of the game. However, the 49ers now face a massive challenge this week when they take on the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings on Sunday night in Minneapolis. The matchup could have major implications for the NFC’s No. 1 seed, which comes with a first-round bye and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs. item.title: Belarusian Tennis Star Aryna Sabalenka Apologizes for Explicit Outburst During Loss to Ukrainian Elina Svitolina
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka, Elina Svitolina Credit: Crystal Li/Alamy NEED TO KNOW Aryna Sabalenka is apologizing for comments she made during a match at the WTA Finals The Belarusian player let fly an expletive-laced tirade regarding Ukraine Sabalenka was playing Ukrainian player Elina Svitolina at the time Aryna Sabalenka is apologizing after she let fly critical comments about Ukraine during her match against Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals. In a video that was widely circulated on social media, Sabalenka unleashed an expletive-laced tirade. In the clip, the Belarusian tennis star, 28, appeared to say “Those f------ Ukrainians, for f---’s sake” in Russian, according to The Athletic . Sabalenka’s voice was not audible in the clip — but in her apology, she clarified that her comments were not directed at the Ukrainian tennis star whom she was playing. Aryna Sabalenka Credit: Mauricio Paiz/NurPhoto/Shutterstock “My comment was not directed at Elina,” Sabalenka wrote on Instagram Saturday, Nov. 14. “I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.” She continued, “That said, I should have handled my frustration differently and I apologize to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.” Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Svitolina, 32, went on to win the group stage match, 6-3, 3-6, 6-1, and advanced to the semis where she dispatched Linda Nosková, 6-2, 6-1. The four-time majors semifinalist then lost to Mirra Andreeva in the final on Sunday, 7-5, 6-3. On Saturday, before the match, Svitolina was asked about Sabalenka’s apology. “There’s many flags and many Ukrainian supporters are here and of course they want me to win in this particular match,” Svitolina said. She continued, “I have seen the glimpse of it because obviously it’s in the social media, but yeah, I just hope the matches between us are respected. Sometimes in some matches there are not great comments towards me in regards of the war. It is like this in the social media sometimes that things are turned around a little bit.” Read the original article on People

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” the sporting director, Ole Book, said to Sky after a week which had contained Der Klassiker in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory against Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.” Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
